# Control API

<!-- Generated by scripts/render-control-api.mjs through scripts/render-tool-reference.mjs; do not edit by hand. -->

Version **1.0.0**. The tools a desktop app — or a script — drives AI Dev with: the state of the
install, setting it up, the local model, the AI clients connected to it, its logs, its settings, and an overview
of the work. They are MCP tools like the others, served by the same daemon, and they make up the `control`
profile, which is opt-in: a session lists them only when it names it (`AI_DEV_PROFILES=control`, alone or with
others). A client that knows a tool's name can call it in any session.

## Connecting

- From a program: `DaemonClientTransport` (`src/core/daemon-transport.mjs`) with the MCP SDK's `Client` finds
  or starts the daemon of the install and proves itself with the descriptor's secret; `profiles: "control"`
  lists these tools. The session runs in the environment the transport is given, as a client's does.
- From a client config: `ai-dev mcp` with `AI_DEV_PROFILES=control` in its environment.

## Conventions

- **Answers.** Every answer is JSON in the text content and, the same, in `structuredContent.result`. Each tool
  advertises the schema below as its `outputSchema`, so an MCP SDK client checks every answer against it.
- **Versions.** `system_status` answers `api_version`. A new optional field, a new tool or a new value of an
  open string is a minor change; a removed, retyped or newly required field is a major one. Objects may carry
  fields this document does not list: read the ones you know.
- **Errors.** A refused call — a wrong argument, a missing `confirm` — answers `isError: true` with the reason
  as its text, and changes nothing. An unknown argument is refused, not ignored.
- **Progress and cancelling.** The long tools (`setup_run`, `model_install`, `model_import`, `model_verify`)
  send `notifications/progress` when the request carries a `progressToken`, and stop when the client cancels
  the request: what is done is kept (a download continues next time from where it stopped).
- **Read-only and destructive.** Each tool's MCP annotations say so; the list below too.

## `system_status` (read-only)

What state this install is in, in one answer: ok, degraded or failed, and why — the version, where the data is, the process serving it, the local model, the search index, the AI clients connected, the settings' problems and the health checks. The desktop app's tray colour. Read-only.

**Input:**

- `checks` — boolean, optional. Run the health checks (about a second, more while Frontend QA's browser starts); false answers from what is on disk only — what a tray that polls asks for. Default `true`.

**Answer** (`structuredContent.result`):

- `api_version` — string
- `status` — `"ok"`, `"degraded"`, `"failed"`. ok: nothing to do; degraded: works, something is missing; failed: does not work.
- `summary` — string
- `version` — string
- `install` — object
  - `kind` — string
  - `root` — string
  - `vault_root` — string
  - `runtime_root` — string
- `served_by` — object. The process that answered: the daemon every client shares, or a client's own server.
  - `kind` — `"daemon"`, `"process"`
  - `pid` — integer
  - `build` — string, optional
  - `sessions` — integer, optional
  - `started_at` — string, optional
  - `idle_timeout_ms` — integer, optional
- `model` — object. Where the local model stands.
  - `installed` — boolean. Every file is there and matches the manifest.
  - `dir` — string
  - `model` — string
  - `revision` — string
  - `dtype` — string
  - `present` — array of string
  - `missing` — array of string
  - `mismatched` — array of string
  - `partial` — array of objects
    - `file` — string
    - `bytes` — integer
    - `size` — integer or null
  - `supported` — boolean. Whether the ONNX runtime runs on this machine.
  - `support_reason` — string
- `index` — object
  - `exists` — boolean
  - `documents` — integer
  - `dense_documents` — integer
  - `dense_pending` — integer
  - `fresh` — boolean
  - `built_at` — string or null
- `clients` — object
  - `found` — integer
  - `connected` — integer
- `settings_problems` — array of string
- `checks` — array of objects
  - `name` — string
  - `status` — string
  - `summary` — string

## `setup_run`

Build what a fresh install does not ship — the skill registry, its quality report, the search index, the routing benchmark — and, when asked, the local model with its document vectors, Frontend QA, and the AI clients' configs. What is already built and current is skipped. Reports progress; a cancelled run stops after the current piece and keeps what is done.

**Input:**

- `model` — boolean, optional. Also download the local BGE-M3 model (about 600 MB) and embed the documents. Default `false`.
- `frontend_qa` — boolean, optional. Also install the Frontend QA runner's dependencies and its Chromium. Default `false`.
- `clients` — string or array of string, optional. "all" (every client found here), or client names: claude-code, claude-desktop, cursor, vscode, codex, gemini.
- `force` — boolean, optional. Rebuild what is already there. Default `false`.

**Answer** (`structuredContent.result`):

- `succeeded` — boolean. The run finished and nothing in it failed: false when it was cancelled, or a step or a client failed.
- `cancelled` — boolean
- `steps` — array of objects
  - `id` — string
  - `title` — string
  - `status` — `"done"`, `"skipped"`, `"failed"`
  - `reason` — string, optional. Why it ran or did not, or what it did.
  - `error` — string, optional
  - `duration_ms` — integer, optional
- `clients` — array of objects or null

## `model_install`

Download the local search model, checksum-verified, continuing a download that was cut off, through the mirror in the settings or AI_DEV_MODEL_MIRROR and the session's proxy. Reports bytes and speed; a cancelled download keeps what it fetched. Does not embed the documents: setup_run with model does, or rebuild_search_index.

**Input:**

No arguments.

**Answer** (`structuredContent.result`):

- `ready` — boolean. The model is complete and verified after this call.
- `dir` — string
- `present` — array of string
- `missing` — array of string
- `mismatched` — array of string
- `model` — object. Where the local model stands.
  - `installed` — boolean. Every file is there and matches the manifest.
  - `dir` — string
  - `model` — string
  - `revision` — string
  - `dtype` — string
  - `present` — array of string
  - `missing` — array of string
  - `mismatched` — array of string
  - `partial` — array of objects
    - `file` — string
    - `bytes` — integer
    - `size` — integer or null
  - `supported` — boolean. Whether the ONNX runtime runs on this machine.
  - `support_reason` — string

## `model_import`

Put the local model in place from a folder or a .zip you already have (another machine, a USB stick), checked file by file against the pinned manifest. Reports progress; cancellable.

**Input:**

- `source` — string. An absolute path to a folder or a .zip holding the model's files.

**Answer** (`structuredContent.result`):

- `ready` — boolean. The model is complete and verified after this call.
- `dir` — string
- `present` — array of string
- `missing` — array of string
- `mismatched` — array of string
- `model` — object. Where the local model stands.
  - `installed` — boolean. Every file is there and matches the manifest.
  - `dir` — string
  - `model` — string
  - `revision` — string
  - `dtype` — string
  - `present` — array of string
  - `missing` — array of string
  - `mismatched` — array of string
  - `partial` — array of objects
    - `file` — string
    - `bytes` — integer
    - `size` — integer or null
  - `supported` — boolean. Whether the ONNX runtime runs on this machine.
  - `support_reason` — string

## `model_verify` (read-only)

Hash every file of the local model against the pinned manifest. Reports progress; cancellable. Read-only.

**Input:**

No arguments.

**Answer** (`structuredContent.result`):

- `ready` — boolean
- `dir` — string
- `present` — array of string
- `missing` — array of string
- `mismatched` — array of string

## `model_remove` (destructive)

Delete the local model's files. Dense search stops until it is installed again; word search goes on. Only the model's own files are removed.

**Input:**

- `confirm` — boolean. Must be true: the files are gone afterwards.

**Answer** (`structuredContent.result`):

- `dir` — string
- `removed` — array of string
- `kept` — array of string
- `freed_bytes` — integer

## `clients_list` (read-only)

Every MCP client this machine can have — Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, Gemini — whether it is installed, and what its ai-dev entry runs: this install, another one, Docker, the 2.x name, or nothing. Read-only.

**Input:**

No arguments.

**Answer** (`structuredContent.result`):

- `clients` — array of objects
  - `client` — string
  - `label` — string
  - `file` — string
  - `found` — boolean. The client is installed here.
  - `connected` — boolean. Its config runs this install of ai-dev.
  - `entry` — string. What its ai-dev entry runs: this install, another one, the 2.x name, Docker, or none.
  - `error` — string, optional

## `clients_install`

Connect AI clients to this install: write the ai-dev entry into their configs (and take out ai-dev-system, the 2.x name). Each changed file keeps its previous bytes beside it. A client reads its config when it starts.

**Input:**

- `clients` — string or array of string, optional. "all" (every client found here), or client names: claude-code, claude-desktop, cursor, vscode, codex, gemini. Default `"all"`.
- `dry_run` — boolean, optional. Say what would change, write nothing. Default `false`.

**Answer** (`structuredContent.result`):

- `results` — array of objects
  - `client` — string. claude-code, claude-desktop, cursor, vscode, codex or gemini.
  - `label` — string
  - `file` — string
  - `status` — string. added, updated, unchanged, removed, restored, absent, skipped or failed; with dry_run, would-add, would-update, would-remove or would-restore.
  - `backup` — string or null, optional
  - `reason` — string, optional
  - `error` — string, optional
- `changed` — integer
- `failed` — integer

## `clients_remove` (destructive)

Disconnect AI clients: take the ai-dev entry out of their configs; a file nothing else touched since goes back byte for byte.

**Input:**

- `clients` — string or array of string, optional. Which clients; every config ai-dev could be in when left out.
- `confirm` — boolean, optional. Must be true, unless dry_run is.
- `dry_run` — boolean, optional. Say what would change, write nothing. Default `false`.

**Answer** (`structuredContent.result`):

- `results` — array of objects
  - `client` — string. claude-code, claude-desktop, cursor, vscode, codex or gemini.
  - `label` — string
  - `file` — string
  - `status` — string. added, updated, unchanged, removed, restored, absent, skipped or failed; with dry_run, would-add, would-update, would-remove or would-restore.
  - `backup` — string or null, optional
  - `reason` — string, optional
  - `error` — string, optional
- `changed` — integer
- `failed` — integer

## `logs_tail` (read-only)

The last lines of a log in the runtime home's logs folder — the daemon's by default. Read-only.

**Input:**

- `log` — string, optional. daemon, daemon.1 (the part set aside at 1 MB), or another log's file name. Default `"daemon"`.
- `lines` — integer, optional. Default `200`.

**Answer** (`structuredContent.result`):

- `log` — string
- `file` — string
- `exists` — boolean
- `size` — integer
- `lines` — array of string
- `truncated` — boolean. Earlier lines exist that are not in this answer.

## `settings_get` (read-only)

The settings the desktop app changes, from ~/.ai-dev/config.json: each value in force — an environment variable's where one overrides the file — where it comes from (default, the file, or that variable), the file's own values, what each setting means, and any stored value that is not valid. Read-only.

**Input:**

No arguments.

**Answer** (`structuredContent.result`):

- `file` — string
- `schema_version` — integer
- `settings` — object
- `sources` — object. Per setting: default, file, or environment (NAME) when a variable overrides the file.
- `problems` — array of string
- `definitions` — array of objects
  - `name` — string
  - `type` — `"string"`, `"number"`, `"boolean"`
  - `default` — any
  - `env` — string or null
  - `description` — string

## `settings_set`

Change settings: each value is checked first, and nothing is written when one is wrong; null puts a setting back to its default. Clients and commands started afterwards use them; a variable set in a client's environment still wins.

**Input:**

- `settings` — object. Settings to change: projects_root, profiles, model_mirror, model_dir, daemon_idle_minutes, daemon_autostart, language.

**Answer** (`structuredContent.result`):

- `changed` — array of string
- `settings` — object
- `note` — string

## `workspace_overview` (read-only)

The work at a glance: the registered projects, the tasks open and lately finished, the epics and how far each has come, the latest decisions, and what the work has cost. Read-only.

**Input:**

- `limit` — integer, optional. How many tasks, epics and decisions to list. Default `10`.

**Answer** (`structuredContent.result`):

- `projects` — array of objects
  - `id` — string
  - `name` — string
  - `root` — string
  - `stack` — array of string
  - `updated_at` — string
- `tasks` — object
  - `active` — array of objects
    - `task_id` — string
    - `title` — string
    - `status` — string
    - `project` — string
    - `updated_at` — string
  - `recent` — array of objects
    - `task_id` — string
    - `title` — string
    - `status` — string
    - `project` — string
    - `updated_at` — string
- `epics` — array of objects
  - `epic_id` — string
  - `title` — string
  - `status` — string
  - `children` — integer
  - `done` — integer
- `decisions` — array of objects
  - `id` — string
  - `title` — string
  - `status` — string
  - `date` — string
  - `project` — string
- `usage` — object
  - `events` — integer
  - `tool_calls` — integer
  - `cost_usd` — number
  - `today_cost_usd` — number
  - `last_7_days_cost_usd` — number
